comment: Retrieval cases over THIS repository. Each query is a question a developer actually asks, and `expect` names the file(s) that answer it. Ground truth was established by reading the code, not by running the retriever — a benchmark scored by the thing it measures is not a benchmark. Unlike benchmarks/ground-truth in physis-core, these queries are deliberately LEXICALLY DISJOINT from their answers where possible: the question uses the words a person would use, the code uses the words a compiler needs. That gap is what a lexical hash cannot cross and a semantic model can.

cases.query: how does the engine pick which embedding model to use, and how does it refuse one that loads but produces nonsense
what stops a word-counting fake from being mistaken for a model that understands meaning
which subcommands are allowed to run on a machine that has not paid, and where is that decided
how is the prompt kept from overflowing the window no matter how large the corpus grows
what happens to the comparison against a larger reference system when nobody has supplied credentials for it
how are near-duplicate documents grouped and statements that disagree with each other flagged
when a phrase was never seen at full length, how is a probability still produced from shorter fragments
how does the system make sure a downloaded weights file was not tampered with before it is used
how does an external coding assistant discover and invoke the capabilities this program offers
how is a customer prevented from editing their own permissions file to unlock paid features
